solea.name: Soléa Aesthetics
solea.overviewHeading: A refined visual identity for a modern aesthetic clinic.
solea.overview: Soléa Aesthetics is a London clinic for subtle, natural-looking treatments. The brand had to earn trust before anyone books: calm and professional, but warm enough to feel personal. We built the identity around a custom-lettered wordmark with a delicate accent on the é, an interlaced SA monogram and an embossed pattern, set in a palette of ivory, stone, taupe, mocha and espresso. The system carries through the treatment menu, aftercare and appointment cards, packaging, social content and a London Underground campaign: Subtle enhancements. Real confidence.

blocks.label: Identity
blocks.note: Custom lettering, an interlaced SA monogram and an earthy palette: calm, reassuring and premium.

blocks.label: In the world
blocks.note: From a gloved hand holding the card to a poster on the Underground.

355.overviewHeading: A quiet, confident identity for an invitation-only community.
355.overview: 355 is a members' community built on curated gatherings and genuine connection. The brand had to feel exclusive without being cold — an understated assurance that rewards the people already inside. We treated the number itself as the icon: spare, memorable, a little mysterious. A dark, tactile palette and refined type run from membership cards to invitations to the web, so every touchpoint feels like part of the same room — earned, considered, and unmistakably for members.

blocks.label: The System
blocks.note: Dark, tactile and refined — a brand that signals belonging, not status.

intellimation.name: intellimation.ai
intellimation.overviewHeading: Building a modern enterprise identity for the future of Vertical AI.
intellimation.overview: intellimation.ai builds proprietary, vertical AI for banking and financial services — automation purpose-built for an industry that runs on trust. The company needed a brand that could stand next to institutions like Barclays, Citi and Nomura without inheriting their stiffness: credible, modern, and clear about a complex product. We built the identity, the message system and a full suite of collateral — website, brochures, presentation decks and a live exhibition presence. The result is one coherent enterprise identity that makes advanced AI feel considered, legible and ready for the room it is selling into.

blocks.label: Print & Collateral
blocks.note: A full system of brochures and one-pagers that make a complex product easy to hand over.

blocks.label: Identity & Stationery
blocks.note: Considered details — the folder, the deck, the print in a client's hands.

blocks.label: Merch & Extras
blocks.note: Details that travel — business cards, a conference badge and a branded polo.

seereen.name: Seereen
seereen.overviewHeading: A calm, confident identity for a modern hair & aesthetics studio.
seereen.overview: Seereen is a hair and aesthetics studio built on care and craft. It needed an identity that felt premium without turning cold — somewhere you would trust with how you look and enjoy walking into. We created the wordmark, a warm and sunlit visual system, and print collateral that leads with real faces and real results. From salon signage to price cards to social, every touchpoint now carries the same quiet welcome — approachable, feminine and unmistakably its own.

blocks.label: Visual Identity
blocks.note: A warm, lowercase wordmark and a sunlit palette set the tone.

opa-taverne.name: Opa Taverne
opa-taverne.overviewHeading: Bottling the warmth of a Mediterranean table into a brand.
opa-taverne.overview: Opa Taverne is a Mediterranean taverna where food, family and long evenings are the whole point. The brand had to carry that warmth off the plate and onto every menu, sign and post — inviting, generous, never touristy. We built a hand-made, hospitable identity in earthy tones and tactile materials, designed to be touched and kept. From the door to the table to Instagram, it now feels like the same welcome you get the moment you walk in.

blocks.label: The Identity
blocks.note: Warm, tactile and hospitable — a brand designed to be touched and kept.

ame.name: AMË
ame.overviewHeading: Heritage, worn forward — an Albanian identity for the street.
ame.overview: AMË is a heritage streetwear label that carries Albanian identity onto the streets of London and beyond. It had to feel proud without being nostalgic — rooted in origin, but cut for now. We anchored the brand in a single idea, origin as identity, and expressed it through the eagle motif, a confident wordmark and a muted, editorial palette. Photography set on rain-slick streets gives it the attitude: understated, self-assured, unmistakably its own — heritage you want to wear.

blocks.label: Art Direction
blocks.note: Rain-slick streets and a muted palette give the label its edge without raising its voice.

her-club.name: HER CLUB
her-club.overviewHeading: Where ambition meets sisterhood — a warm, elevated identity.
her-club.overview: HER Club is a community where ambitious women connect and grow together. The brand needed to feel both aspirational and intimate — polished enough to trust, warm enough to join. We built it around warmth and understated assurance: soft golds, refined type and a crest that signals belonging without exclusion. From welcome cards to membership collateral to the web, every piece feels personal — a hand extended, not a gate kept. The result reads as elevated and generous at once.

blocks.label: The Identity
blocks.note: Soft golds and a refined crest — belonging, without a gate.

vs-2026.name: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2026
vs-2026.overviewHeading: Victoria’s Secret’s greatest asset isn’t lingerie. It’s anticipation.
vs-2026.overview: Within 24 hours of the 18 October 2026 show in Los Angeles, we tracked how Victoria’s Secret turned a runway into a multi-channel marketing event. We collected public data from YouTube, TikTok, Instagram and Google Search, compared it like-for-like with 2025, and separated what the numbers show from what they only suggest. The result: the show is the finale of a 25-day content series, not a one-night broadcast. It is built on anticipation, backstage access and one unmistakable visual language, with a shop placed next to every moment.

blocks.label: The question
blocks.note: How does Victoria’s Secret turn a fashion show into a multi-channel marketing event, and what can smaller brands learn from its approach to attention, influence and commerce?

items.v: 144 brand TikToks in 25 days, 85 of them more than 24 hours before the show. A six-episode casting docuseries reached 19.4M YouTube views before the runway.
The official YouTube stream had 10.3M views after 3.3 hours and 21.0M after 20.5 hours: about 13% ahead of 2025 at the same point (range −2% to +16%).
Likes per view fell from 0.050 to 0.031. Worldwide Google searches for the show were 44% below 2025 on show day (US −7%, UK +12%) even as views rose.

The most-viewed TikToks were pre-show backstage clips, two led by legacy Angels (11.1M, 9.8M). Kylie Jenner’s Fantasy Bra post drew the most Instagram conversation: 35K comments vs 20K at ~3M likes each.
An official After Party LIVE on TikTok Shop started straight after the show, and the site led with “Shop the Fashion Show”.

blocks.label: The wait is the product
blocks.note: Countdowns, a withheld reveal and a serialised casting story turned three weeks of waiting into content. Anticipation, curiosity and narrative transportation are well-documented drivers of value. The data here is consistent with them; it does not prove they caused the result.

blocks.label: Celebrity buys talk. Heritage buys reach.
blocks.note: Kylie Jenner wore the 2026 Fantasy Bra by Jacob & Co. (estimated $50M, per Vogue). Her post led on comments and search interest, while legacy Angels led on views. Her commercial terms were not disclosed.

blocks.label: One show. Dozens of doors.
blocks.note: Live on YouTube, TikTok, Instagram and in AMC cinemas, then 15 YouTube uploads and 44 TikToks in the next 20 hours: one broadcast cut into many entry points.

blocks.label: What the public data can’t tell us

items.v: How many sales the show drove, and how many viewers became buyers. VS&Co reports the quarter that includes the show around December 2026.
Whether the show earned back its cost. Production, talent and media spend are not public.
How many unique people it reached. Views overlap across platforms and repeat viewers.
How much of Kylie’s buzz turned into revenue. That needs first-party data and a brand-lift test.
19 October 2026, 19:15–20:35 BST, 19.5–21 hours after the livestream began. Every count is a snapshot that keeps growing.

35 official YouTube videos, 144 TikTok posts, 12 Instagram posts, Google Trends (2025 and 2026 normalised together), Internet Archive captures of the 2025 stream, VS&Co investor releases and trade press.
Views are not unique viewers and are never summed across platforms. Trends values are relative indices, not search counts. Company figures are labelled as company-reported.
